basis: Spring Security is STATELESS and the console accepts only an explicit validated Authorization bearer token.
No form login, HTTP Basic, OAuth2 login, authentication cookie, servlet-session authentication, query-token or form-token path is active.
SignedBearerIdentityIT proves cookie/query/form/session inputs cannot authenticate, no Set-Cookie/session is produced, and hostile Origin mutation is refused even with a valid bearer.
reassessment_triggers: cookie or servlet-session authentication is introduced
form login, HTTP Basic, OAuth2 login or another browser-ambient credential is introduced
bearer transport or CORS/Origin policy changes
the negative signed-bearer integration contract is removed or weakened
alerts.dismissed_comment: False positive. This API is bearer-only and STATELESS: cookies, query/form tokens and servlet sessions cannot authenticate; no auth cookie/session is issued; hostile-Origin mutation is refused. Reassess if ambient auth or CORS/Origin rules change.

basis: The empty value is an inactive override under spring.flyway.enabled=false.
It clears the inherited migration-secret placeholder from the serving application process; it is not an application or migration credential.
The serving process receives only the application-role credential, while the separate managed migration executable requires its own credential and attestation envelope.
ApplicationConfigurationTest.rolesAreSeparated and packaged migration tests pin this separation.
reassessment_triggers: in-application Flyway is enabled in staging or production
the serving application receives a migration-role credential
the separate migration executable/credential boundary changes
the configuration invariant test is removed or weakened
alerts.dismissed_comment: False positive. Production disables in-app Flyway; this empty value only clears the inherited migration-secret placeholder. The server gets only the app-role secret; a separate migration runner uses its own credential. Reassess if that boundary changes.

basis: The flagged setEntity call is Apache HttpUriRequestBase for an outgoing provider request, not a servlet/browser response sink.
HTML escaping would corrupt provider request bytes and their digest binding.
The outbound layer enforces HTTPS, allowlisted destination/method/path/headers, pinned public DNS, no redirects/cookies/retries, and body/response bounds.
BoundedOutboundHttpTest observes exact markup-containing bytes only on a local transport fixture while public preparation still rejects unsafe destinations.
reassessment_triggers: the value is rendered into a servlet/browser response or HTML page
the outgoing request abstraction is replaced by a browser-facing sink
destination, DNS, redirect, header or size controls are weakened
alerts.dismissed_comment: False positive. The sink is Apache HttpUriRequestBase.setEntity for an outbound provider request, not browser output. Exact bytes are required; HTTPS, destination, DNS, redirect, header and size controls remain enforced. Reassess if bytes are rendered to users.

basis: The user-controlled part-number condition is a denying guard that throws and returns no data.
Every successful path resolves stored requester/organization ownership and live store scope, then calls the DB authorization function before storage I/O.
The service reauthorizes after I/O before returning bytes.
DiagnosticExportIT covers invalid parts, foreign IDs, revoked access and expired jobs.
reassessment_triggers: an invalid-part branch can continue or return data
stored requester/organization or live scope checks are removed
pre-I/O or post-I/O database authorization is removed or moved after response
alerts.dismissed_comment: False positive. The part-number branch denies invalid input and returns no data. Successful reads require stored ownership/live scope, DB authorization before I/O, and DB reauthorization after I/O. Reassess if the guard or authorization sequence changes.

basis: The integrity condition throws on length/hash mismatch and returns no bytes.
A successful response requires authorization before I/O, exact custody length/hash verification, and database reauthorization after I/O.
Revocation during object read returns forbidden and does not write a PART_VERIFIED audit event.
reassessment_triggers: integrity failure can return any bytes
successful audit is moved before integrity and authorization checks
alerts.dismissed_comment: False positive. Length/hash mismatch returns no bytes. Success requires pre-I/O DB authorization, exact custody integrity checks, and post-I/O DB reauthorization; mid-read revocation is refused. Reassess if integrity or authorization order changes.
